title: Typed catch for PipelineStoppedException is unreliable — must use bare catch with type check
description: In PowerShell, System.Management.Automation.PipelineStoppedException is a flow-control exception that functions as a pipeline shutdown signal. When a scriptblock is invoked as a .NET event handler delegate (e.g. WinForms Timer Tick, Add_Click), the PowerShell runtime compiles the block into a lambda. Inside that lambda, typed catch blocks (catch [PipelineStoppedException]) are NOT reliably honored by the runtime — the exception can bypass the typed catch and propagate to the calling native code (WndProc), causing a visible crash and no useful stack trace. The only reliable containment is a bare catch {} block with an explicit -is type check inside. This pattern was the root cause of the PipelineStoppedException crash in Start-LocalWebEngineService.ps1 -Action Start (2026-05-22).
ps_version_scope_note: The bypass is most reproducible in PS 5.1 Desktop WinForms context. PS7 Core may behave differently but bare-catch is still safer.
detection_method: Regex scan for typed catch of PipelineStoppedException in PS1/PSM1 files
exception_stack_highlight: at lambda_method(Closure, Object, EventArgs) at System.Windows.Forms.Timer.TimerNativeWindow.WndProc(Message& m)
trusted_fix_notes: Applied in Start-LocalWebEngineService.ps1 $updateState handler (2026-05-22). Bare catch + -is type check + timer.Stop() + ExitThread(). Parser validated OK.

known_instances.risk: CRITICAL — caused PipelineStoppedException crash on -Action start
